title: Over-squashing as Transport Congestion: A Sandpile Dynamics Perspective

problem.claim: MP-GNN performance drops on tasks requiring long-range interactions because over-squashing causes exponential information compression in fixed-width embeddings.

gap.claim: Existing analyses often explain over-squashing through geometric bottlenecks under linear diffusion assumptions, which does not account for thresholded nonlinearities in GNNs.

contributions.claim: The work uses the discrete sandpile model as a structural proxy to characterize stabilization-invariant equivalence classes and derive cut-based lower bounds linking graph bottlenecks to unavoidable stabilization effort.
The theory identifies capacity and cut size as relevant design factors for stabilization cost and transport congestion.
The work proposes a differentiable Sandpile Stabilization Layer and congestion-aware objectives to redistribute excess load and manage stabilization costs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on long-range benchmarks, together with congestion and collision diagnostics, are reported to show that targeting sandpile-identified bottlenecks mitigates representation collapse and improves over standard baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: MP-GNNs are widely used for relational data.
Long-range tasks suffer from over-squashing caused by exponential information compression in fixed-width embeddings.
The work reframes the issue through thresholded nonlinearities and an Abelian-sandpile-like load-release view.
A discrete sandpile proxy yields bottleneck-related stabilization results and motivates a differentiable stabilization layer with congestion-aware objectives.
Experiments and diagnostics are reported to show mitigation of representation collapse and improvement over standard baselines.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links graph bottlenecks to high stabilization cost and transport congestion.

interpretation.claim: Analyzing information propagation as a load-management problem may expose design factors that geometric diffusion analyses miss.

application.claim: For long-range message passing, inspect capacity and cut size and consider objectives that redistribute excess intermediate load.

exception.claim: The theory is discrete while the implementation is a continuous vector-valued surrogate, so theoretical conclusions may not transfer directly without further analysis.

unknowns: Specific long-range benchmark datasets and task settings are not provided.
Quantitative results, metric values, and baseline identities are not provided.
The continuous surrogate's implementation details and its relationship to the discrete theory are not specified.
